Key Research Thinking Patterns: Hybrid Generative-Discriminative Frameworks: Integrating generative models like WGAN-GP with discriminative classifiers (e.g., XGBoost, CNNs) to enhance data efficiency and diagnostic accuracy in medical imaging and photonic design.

Multimodal Graph and Attention-Based Fusion: Leveraging advanced architectures such as Multi-View Graph Convolution Networks (MVS-GCN) and Hierarchical Transformers to synthesize heterogeneous data sources including MRI, genomics, and clinical records for complex disease progression modeling.

Physics-Informed and Constraint-Driven Inverse Design: Applying digital twin simulations and physical constraints within optimization loops (e.g., XG-Attention-WGAN PIC framework) to discover novel geometries for microring resonators and photonic components.

Positive-Unlabeled Learning for Sparse Data Domains: Utilizing PU classification strategies and self-supervised learning techniques to address label scarcity and synthesizability prediction challenges in computational materials science and rare disease detection.
Summary Description: Mike Banad specializes in the intersection of Artificial Intelligence and advanced engineering systems, spanning Smart Grids, Integrated Photonics, Medical Imaging, and Computational Materials Science. His research synthesizes foundational machine learning paradigms with emerging technologies like Digital Twins, Large Language Models, and Generative Adversarial Networks. He employs hybrid architectures to address critical challenges such as data privacy, computational scalability, and inverse design optimization. His work emphasizes resilience-centric optimization for power networks, high-fidelity geometry discovery for photonic components, and multimodal diagnostic pipelines for neurodegenerative diseases using data from major consortia like ADNI and OASIS. Recently, he has expanded into materials informatics, developing the SyntheFormer framework to predict the synthesizability of inorganic crystals, demonstrating a versatile approach to complex, high-dimensional parameter spaces across diverse physical and biological domains.
